subs.label: Action & Battle Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the fighting engine and its tradition: shōnen power battles first, then contest, school and urban-fantasy forms, adult and martial traditions, heroes, street and gun action, military last

leaves.label: Battle Shōnen
leaves.defn: A long-running shōnen serial whose engine is an escalating ladder of fights inside a power system, with a hero who grows through rivals, training arcs and tournaments (One Piece, Hunter x Hunter, Fairy Tail, Fullmetal Alchemist). If the powers are ki-based martial arts it goes to C1-9; if the foes are demons, yōkai or curses, to C1-2.
leaves.see: C1-2 Supernatural Battle Shōnen; C1-9 Martial Arts Anime; C3 Fantasy & Isekai Anime
leaves.axis: by the world the fights happen in: sea and quest worlds first, then fantasy kingdoms, then modern cities, contest formats last

leaves.label: Supernatural Battle Shōnen
leaves.defn: A battle shōnen whose fighters hunt or channel the supernatural, shinigami, yōkai, demons, curses, as an organised calling (Bleach, Kimetsu no Yaiba, Jujutsu Kaisen, InuYasha). Vampire hunting goes to C1-7; adult splatter to C1-8.
leaves.see: C1-1 Battle Shōnen; C1-7 Vampire Anime; C9 Horror Anime
leaves.axis: by the kind of spirit fought: the afterlife first, then yōkai and demons, then curses and exorcism

leaves.label: Superpower Anime (chōnōryoku)
leaves.defn: Action whose combatants are espers or ability users with one personal power each, and whose drama is the rules of those powers (JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken, Toaru Kagaku no Railgun, Bungou Stray Dogs, Darker than Black). Costumed hero work goes to C1-13.
leaves.see: C1-13 Superhero Anime; C1-1 Battle Shōnen
leaves.axis: by how the powers are organised: one-to-one ability duels, then esper cities, then agencies and syndicates, then hunted test subjects

leaves.label: Battle Royale & Death Game Anime
leaves.defn: Action built on an enclosed, rule-bound contest in which participants must kill or be eliminated until one survives (Fate/Zero, Gantz, Darwin's Game, Juuni Taisen). An open tournament without killing goes to C1-9.
leaves.aliases: death game (desu gēmu), Holy Grail War
leaves.see: C8 Drama, Mystery & Psychological Anime; C1-3 Superpower Anime
leaves.axis: by the contest: the Holy Grail War franchise first, then other kill-or-die games

leaves.label: Battle School Anime
leaves.defn: A school or academy series, usually from a light novel, in which students rank, duel and graduate by combat magic or weapons (Mahouka Koukou no Rettousei, Rakudai Kishi no Cavalry, Gakusen Toshi Asterisk, Kill la Kill). A school setting in a Jump battle serial stays in C1-1.
leaves.aliases: gakuen battle, battle academy, magic high school
leaves.see: C1-6 Urban Fantasy Action; C5 Romance Anime
leaves.axis: by what the hierarchy rests on: magic-school rankings first, then duel-harem and uniform-weapon academies

leaves.label: Urban Fantasy Action
leaves.defn: Action in which a hidden magical or otherworldly order breaks into the contemporary city and ordinary teens fight it, chiefly from light novels and games (Shakugan no Shana, Persona 4 the Animation, Ore dake Level Up na Ken, X). Shōnen-magazine demon hunting goes to C1-2.
leaves.see: C1-2 Supernatural Battle Shōnen; C3 Fantasy & Isekai Anime
leaves.axis: by what breaks in: hidden magic among us, then dungeon gates and hunters, then demon and otherworld incursions

leaves.label: Vampire Anime
leaves.defn: Action whose fighters are vampires or vampire hunters and whose conflict is the war between the undead and the living (Hellsing Ultimate, Strike the Blood, Owari no Seraph, Blade).
leaves.see: C1-2 Supernatural Battle Shōnen; C9 Horror Anime

leaves.label: Seinen Action Anime
leaves.defn: Adult-demographic action whose fights are graphic, its heroes monstrous or compromised, and its tone nihilist (Tokyo Ghoul, Ajin, Terra Formars, Akame ga Kill!). Horror without a fighting engine goes to C9.
leaves.see: C9 Horror Anime; C1-2 Supernatural Battle Shōnen

leaves.label: Martial Arts Anime
leaves.defn: Anime whose fights are bodily martial technique, ki, styles and lineages, contested in duels and tournaments (Dragon Ball Z, Grappler Baki, Hokuto no Ken, Saint Seiya). Weapon-based Japanese swordsmanship goes to C1-11; Chinese martial worlds to C1-12.
leaves.see: C1-1 Battle Shōnen; C1-12 Wuxia & Xianxia Animation; A7 Action & Martial Arts
leaves.axis: by the fighting tradition: ki power-escalation first, then armoured warriors, tournaments, game adaptations, school brawlers and the post-apocalyptic fist

leaves.label: Ninja Anime
leaves.defn: Anime whose fighters are shinobi using ninjutsu or ninpō, historical or modern (Naruto, Basilisk: Kouga Ninpou Chou, Juubee Ninpuuchou, Nabari no Ou).
leaves.see: C1-11 Samurai & Chanbara Anime; C1-1 Battle Shōnen
leaves.axis: by setting: the Naruto franchise first, then historical ninpō duels, then modern ninja

leaves.label: Samurai & Chanbara Anime
leaves.defn: A jidaigeki in animation: swordsmen of feudal or Bakumatsu Japan whose engine is the blade duel (Rurouni Kenshin, Samurai Champloo, Shigurui, Hakuouki). Ninja go to C1-10.
leaves.see: C1-10 Ninja Anime; A8 Historical & Period Film
leaves.axis: by era and engine: wandering swordsmen first, then Bakumatsu and Shinsengumi, Sengoku warlords, supernatural jidaigeki, battle-shōnen jidaigeki

leaves.label: Wuxia & Xianxia Animation
leaves.defn: Chinese animation (donghua) of the martial world (wuxia) or of Daoist cultivation toward immortality (xianxia), including modern-city cultivation (Mo Dao Zu Shi, Doupo Cangqiong, Scissor Seven, Yi Ren Zhi Xia).
leaves.see: C1-9 Martial Arts Anime; C3 Fantasy & Isekai Anime
leaves.axis: by the martial world: jianghu wuxia first, then xianxia cultivation epics, then modern-city cultivation

leaves.label: Superhero Anime
leaves.defn: Anime about costumed or transforming heroes who protect the public, including hero societies, henshin teams, deconstructions and American comics made in Japan (Boku no Hero Academia, One Punch Man, Tiger & Bunny, Kagaku Ninja-tai Gatchaman). Tokusatsu-derived giant heroes go to C2-5.
leaves.see: C1-3 Superpower Anime; C2-5 Tokusatsu & Kaiju Anime
leaves.axis: by the hero tradition: hero society first, then henshin and cyborg teams, parody and deconstruction, American comics

leaves.label: Delinquent Anime (yankī)
leaves.defn: Anime about high-school delinquents and bōsōzoku gangs whose engine is the street brawl and gang loyalty (Tokyo Revengers, Wind Breaker, Beelzebub).
leaves.see: C1-9 Martial Arts Anime; C10 Comedy Anime

leaves.label: Gun Action Anime
leaves.defn: Action whose engine is gunplay by hitmen, sweepers, mercenaries or armed heroines (Black Lagoon, City Hunter, Noir, Lycoris Recoil). Military units go to C1-17; cyborg police to C2-8.
leaves.aliases: girls with guns, gun fu, hitman anime
leaves.see: A2 Crime; C1-17 Military Action Anime; C2-8 Cyberpunk Anime
leaves.axis: by who holds the gun: hitmen and sweepers, then girls with guns, then mercenaries and mafia

leaves.label: Spy Anime
leaves.defn: Action whose heroes are secret agents running covert missions (Princess Principal, Spy Kyoushitsu, R.O.D: Read or Die, Yozakura-san Chi no Daisakusen).
leaves.see: C1-15 Gun Action Anime

leaves.label: Military Action Anime
leaves.defn: Action about soldiers, pilots and units in present-day or alternate-history warfare, without mecha or space settings (Area 88, Pumpkin Scissors, Kouya no Kotobuki Hikoutai). Future warfare goes to C2-7.
leaves.see: C2-7 Military Science Fiction Anime; A9 War Film

subs.label: Mecha & Science Fiction Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the science-fiction premise: giant robots first, then tokusatsu, space, war and tech-noir premises, then future societies, time and alien premises, anthologies last

leaves.label: Super Robot
leaves.defn: Mecha anime in which a unique, near-mythic giant robot piloted by a hot-blooded hero fights monsters or invaders, with named attacks and combinations (Mazinger Z, Tengen Toppa Gurren Lagann, Shinseiki Evangelion, Yuusha-Ou GaoGaiGar). Mass-produced machines in a realistic war go to C2-2.
leaves.see: C2-2 Real Robot; C2-5 Tokusatsu & Kaiju Anime
leaves.axis: by the robot's mode: 1970s classics first, then hot-blooded revivals, deconstructions, occult giants, surreal and parody robots

leaves.label: Real Robot
leaves.defn: Mecha anime in which robots are mass-produced weapons or tools in a plausible war or society, with logistics, politics and attrition (Soukou Kihei Votoms, Macross, Code Geass, Kidou Keisatsu Patlabor). The Gundam franchise is C2-3.
leaves.see: C2-3 Gundam; C2-1 Super Robot; C2-7 Military Science Fiction Anime
leaves.axis: by the battlefield: military mecha wars first, then rebellion and politics, transforming fighters, alien wars, police mecha, fantasy-world mecha, teen and comedy mecha

leaves.label: Gundam
leaves.defn: Any entry of Sunrise's Gundam franchise, the founding real-robot saga (Kidou Senshi Gundam, Kidou Senshi Zeta Gundam, Gundam Wing, Kidou Senshi Gundam: Suisei no Majo).
leaves.see: C2-2 Real Robot
leaves.axis: by continuity: the Universal Century first, then alternate universes, then Gunpla battle spin-offs

leaves.label: Mecha Musume
leaves.defn: Anime whose fighters are girls fused with machine parts, warships or aircraft, or girl-shaped machines (Strike Witches, Kantai Collection: KanColle, Aoki Hagane no Arpeggio, Frame Arms Girl).
leaves.see: C2-7 Military Science Fiction Anime; C6 Slice of Life & Iyashikei Anime

leaves.label: Tokusatsu & Kaiju Anime
leaves.defn: Animation of the tokusatsu tradition, giant monsters (kaiju), Ultra-type giant heroes and Kamen Rider-type henshin armour (SSSS.Gridman, Ultraman, Godzilla: Kaijuu Wakusei, Kaijuu 8-gou).
leaves.see: C1-13 Superhero Anime; C2-1 Super Robot

leaves.label: Space Opera Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction set among starships and planets, whose scale is interstellar war, piracy or roaming adventure (Ginga Eiyuu Densetsu, Uchuu Senkan Yamato, Cowboy Bebop, Uchuu Kaizoku Captain Herlock). Space mecha go to C2-1/C2-2.
leaves.see: C2-2 Real Robot; C2-7 Military Science Fiction Anime
leaves.axis: by the voyage: galactic war epics first, then space pirates and wanderers, space westerns and bounty hunters, space adventure and survival

leaves.label: Military Science Fiction Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction about future or alternate-world soldiers, fleets and wars, without giant robots as the core (Last Exile, Blue Gender, Gyakusatsu Kikan, All You Need Is Kill).
leaves.see: C2-2 Real Robot; C1-17 Military Action Anime

leaves.label: Cyberpunk Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction of high tech and low life: cyborgs, networks and megacities policed by corporations and states (Akira, Koukaku Kidoutai, Psycho-Pass, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners).
leaves.see: C2-9 Virtual Reality Anime; C2-11 Dystopian Anime
leaves.axis: by the cyberpunk strand: Ghost in the Shell first, then cyber-police and hardsuits, cyborg and android noir, megacity dystopias

leaves.label: Virtual Reality Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction whose stakes play out inside virtual worlds, games or augmented reality (Accel World, Summer Wars, Dennou Coil, Sword Art Online Alternative: Gun Gale Online). Trapped-in-another-world fantasy goes to C3.
leaves.see: C3 Fantasy & Isekai Anime; C2-8 Cyberpunk Anime

leaves.label: Android & Artificial Intelligence Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction whose subject is robots, androids and AIs as persons (Tetsuwan Atom, Pluto, Eve no Jikan, Vivy: Fluorite Eye's Song). Giant piloted robots go to C2-1/C2-2.
leaves.see: C2-8 Cyberpunk Anime; C2-1 Super Robot

leaves.label: Dystopian Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction of a controlled, unjust future society that its heroes expose or resist (Shinsekai yori, No.6, Harmony, Guilty Crown). Tech-noir megacities go to C2-8.
leaves.see: C2-8 Cyberpunk Anime; C2-12 Post-Apocalyptic Anime

leaves.label: Post-Apocalyptic Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction set after the collapse of civilisation, about surviving, wandering or rebuilding (Kaze no Tani no Nausicaä, Dr. Stone, Shoujo Shuumatsu Ryokou, Casshern Sins). Hokuto no Ken stays in C1-9.
leaves.see: C2-11 Dystopian Anime; C1-9 Martial Arts Anime
leaves.axis: by what follows the fall: rebuilding first, then wasteland action, eco-apocalypse, quiet end-of-world journeys

leaves.label: Time Travel Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction whose plot engine is time travel, time loops or crossing between parallel worlds (Steins;Gate, Toki wo Kakeru Shoujo, Noein, Gnosia).
leaves.see: C8 Drama, Mystery & Psychological Anime

leaves.label: Alien Invasion & First Contact Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction about aliens arriving on Earth, invading, infiltrating, or simply moving in (Kiseijuu: Sei no Kakuritsu, Seikaisuru Kado, Dead Dead Demons Dededede Destruction, Ansatsu Kyoushitsu).
leaves.see: C2-6 Space Opera Anime; C10 Comedy Anime

leaves.label: Hard Science Fiction Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction grounded in plausible physics and engineering, usually of spaceflight and work in orbit (Planetes, Ouritsu Uchuugun: Honneamise no Tsubasa, Chikyuugai Shounen Shoujo).
leaves.see: C2-6 Space Opera Anime

leaves.label: Steampunk Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction of an alternate steam-age technology, airships and clockwork (Steamboy, Fushigi no Umi no Nadia, Sakura Taisen, Clockwork Planet).
leaves.see: C2-2 Real Robot; C1-16 Spy Anime

leaves.label: Science Fiction Anthology Film
leaves.defn: An omnibus of short SF films by several directors under one title (Memories, Robot Carnival, Manie-Manie: Meikyuu Monogatari, Genius Party).
leaves.see: C14 Animated Short; C2-8 Cyberpunk Anime
